name: Campus/Student Group Health Plan (3L cover)
description: The kind of group health policy many Indian colleges and universities arrange (often mandatorily) for enrolled students, typically bundled into fees or offered as an opt-in group scheme via a TPA.
price_basis: approx market range for a college-arranged group student scheme, from general research; actual price is set by the college's tie-up insurer and TPA, not a public retail rate
key_features: Hospitalization cover for illness and accidents during the academic term
Often includes OPD/dispensary visits and ambulance cover
Usually cashless at a TPA network of hospitals
Sometimes bundled with personal accident cover for the student
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing conditions (often with limited or no waiver given short policy terms)
Cosmetic treatment, dental/vision unless specifically covered
Treatment outside the policy period (e.g. during long vacations, in some schemes)
Self-inflicted injury, intoxication-related claims
waiting_period_note: Group/student schemes often have shorter or waived waiting periods versus retail individual plans, but this varies by institution and insurer; always check the specific college policy document

name: Individual Health Insurance (3L cover)
description: An entry-level individual (retail) health insurance policy for a single young adult, covering hospitalization expenses up to 3 lakh rupees.
price_basis: approx market range for an 18-25 year old non-smoker, from general comparison articles and advisory pages
key_features: In-patient hospitalization cover
Pre- and post-hospitalization expense cover (typically 30/60 days)
Cashless treatment at network hospitals
No-claim bonus / cumulative bonus increasing sum insured over renewal years
Daycare procedures covered
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing diseases for an initial waiting period
Cosmetic and dental procedures (non-accident related)
OPD consultations (unless a rider is bought)
Self-inflicted injury, substance abuse related treatment
Experimental or unproven treatments
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years; specific illnesses (e.g. cataract, hernia) often have a 1-2 year waiting period; initial 30-day waiting period for non-accident claims

name: Individual Health Insurance (5L cover)
description: A commonly recommended starting sum-insured tier for a young, healthy adult buying their first individual health policy in India.
price_basis: approx market range for an 18-25 year old non-smoker, from general comparison and advisory articles (not any single insurer's quoted price)
key_features: In-patient hospitalization cover
Pre- and post-hospitalization expense cover
Cashless treatment at a large network of hospitals
Restoration/refill of sum insured after a claim in some plans
No-claim bonus increasing effective cover over time
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing diseases during the waiting period
Cosmetic, dental and vision care not arising from an accident
OPD and routine check-ups (unless rider/add-on purchased)
Maternity (usually excluded or requires a separate waiting period/rider)
Non-allopathic treatment limits unless an AYUSH cover is included
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years; a 30-day initial waiting period applies to most non-accident claims; specific disease waiting periods of 1-2 years are common

name: Individual Health Insurance (10L cover)
description: A higher sum-insured individual plan, increasingly recommended given rising healthcare costs, even for young policyholders, to avoid being underinsured for serious illness.
price_basis: approx market range for an 18-25 year old non-smoker, from general comparison and advisory articles
key_features: Higher in-patient and post-hospitalization cover limits
Wider sub-limits or no sub-limits on room rent in many plans
Cashless network across most major hospitals
Often includes free annual health check-ups
May include modern/advanced treatment cover (e.g. robotic surgery) in some plans
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing diseases during waiting period
Cosmetic and elective procedures
OPD unless an add-on is purchased
Unproven/experimental treatments
Claims arising from war, nuclear risk, or self-inflicted harm
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years; standard 30-day initial waiting period; specific ailment waiting periods of 1-2 years are common

name: Family Floater Health Plan (5L cover)
description: A single policy covering a student and immediate family members (e.g. parents or siblings) under one shared sum insured, often more cost-effective than separate individual policies when the family is young and healthy.
price_basis: approx market range for a young family (2-4 members, youngest adult 18-25) from general comparison articles; premium depends heavily on the eldest member's age
key_features: Shared sum insured usable by any covered family member
Pre- and post-hospitalization cover
Often cheaper per head than buying individual policies for each member
Cashless treatment at network hospitals
No-claim bonus benefits the whole floater
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing diseases during waiting period for each member
Cosmetic and dental procedures
OPD unless rider purchased
One member's large claim can deplete the shared sum insured for the whole family in that year
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years per member; premium and waiting-period terms are generally driven by the oldest insured member's age and health, not the student's

name: Critical Illness Cover
description: A lump-sum payout policy that pays a fixed amount on diagnosis of a listed serious illness (e.g. cancer, major organ failure, stroke), separate from and in addition to a regular hospitalization policy.
price_basis: approx market range for a young adult for a 10L lump-sum critical-illness benefit, from general comparison articles; cheaper entry plans with 1L cover exist for under Rs. 1,500/year
key_features: One-time lump-sum payout on first diagnosis of a covered critical illness
Payout can be used for treatment, income replacement, or any purpose
Usually covers a defined list of illnesses (commonly 8-20+ conditions depending on plan)
Can be bought as a standalone policy or as a rider on a base health policy
typical_exclusions: Illnesses not on the policy's specific covered list
Pre-existing/previously diagnosed conditions
Survival period clause: no payout if the insured does not survive a specified number of days (commonly 15-30 days) after diagnosis
Illnesses diagnosed within the initial waiting period (commonly 90 days)
waiting_period_note: Typically a 90-day initial waiting period from policy start before any diagnosis is payable; survival period clauses (commonly 15-30 days post-diagnosis) also apply

name: Personal Accident Cover
description: A policy that pays a lump sum or income benefit for accidental death, permanent total/partial disability, or (on some plans) temporary total disability — common for students doing internships, travel, sports, or two-wheeler commuting.
price_basis: approx market range for a young adult for roughly 5L accidental cover, from general comparison and advisory articles; personal accident premiums are generally low relative to health cover
key_features: Lump-sum payout for accidental death or permanent disability
Partial payouts on a defined scale for specific disabilities (e.g. loss of limb, eyesight)
Some plans include weekly compensation for temporary total disability
Often available as a rider on a health policy or standalone
Low premium relative to sum insured since it covers accidents only, not illness
typical_exclusions: Death or disability from illness (not accident-related)
Suicide or self-inflicted injury
Accidents while under the influence of alcohol/drugs
Participation in hazardous sports/activities unless specifically covered
War, riot, or nuclear-related incidents
waiting_period_note: Personal accident covers are typically event-based (accident must occur after the policy start date) rather than having long pre-existing-condition style waiting periods

name: OPD / Outpatient Add-on Cover
description: An add-on or rider (rarely sold standalone) that reimburses outpatient expenses not covered by standard hospitalization policies — doctor consultations, diagnostics, pharmacy, and dental/vision check-ups.
price_basis: approx market range for an OPD rider with roughly 10,000-25,000 annual OPD limit, from general comparison articles; pricing varies widely by insurer and sub-limits
key_features: Reimbursement or cashless cover for doctor consultations
Diagnostic tests (blood work, imaging) cover
Pharmacy/medicine expense reimbursement
Dental and vision check-up cover in some plans
Often available only as an add-on to a base individual or family floater policy
typical_exclusions: Cosmetic consultations/treatments
Expenses beyond the annual OPD sub-limit
Alternative medicine consultations unless specifically included
Pre-existing chronic condition management in some plans
waiting_period_note: OPD add-ons commonly have their own waiting period (often 30-90 days) separate from the base policy's hospitalization waiting periods

name: Top-up Health Insurance Plan
description: A policy that activates only after a single hospitalization claim exceeds a defined 'deductible' threshold, used to cheaply raise total cover above a base policy on a per-claim basis.
price_basis: approx market range for a 10L top-up with a deductible of roughly 3-5L, for a young adult, from general comparison articles
key_features: Large additional sum insured at a fraction of an equivalent base policy's premium
Deductible applies per claim/hospitalization event, not cumulatively across the year
Can be combined with an employer-provided or base individual policy
Useful for raising effective cover cheaply once past the deductible threshold
typical_exclusions: Any single claim below the deductible is not paid at all
Pre-existing disease waiting periods similar to base policies
OPD and non-hospitalization expenses
Pre-existing conditions during waiting period
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years, similar to base individual policies; the deductible resets each policy year

name: Super Top-up Health Insurance Plan
description: Similar to a top-up plan but the deductible is applied on an aggregate basis across all hospitalizations in the policy year, not per single claim, making it pay out more readily after multiple smaller claims.
price_basis: approx market range for a 10L super top-up with a deductible of roughly 3-5L, for a young adult, from general comparison and advisory articles
key_features: Deductible is calculated cumulatively across all claims in the policy year, not per event
Large additional sum insured at lower cost than an equivalent full base policy
Commonly recommended as a cost-efficient way to scale up cover over a base/family floater plan
Can often be bought independent of insurer of the base policy
typical_exclusions: Total claims in the year below the aggregate deductible are not paid
Pre-existing disease waiting periods similar to base policies
OPD and non-hospitalization expenses typically excluded
Maternity typically excluded or capped
waiting_period_note: Pre-existing conditions typically excluded for 2-4 years; deductible is tracked on a rolling/aggregate basis for the policy year, resetting at renewal

name: Student Travel/Study-Abroad Health Cover
description: A specialised policy for students travelling or studying outside India, combining overseas medical/hospitalization cover with trip-related benefits (baggage loss, study interruption, sponsor protection) and often required by the destination country's visa process.
price_basis: approx market range for a one-year overseas student health/travel policy, from general study-abroad advisory articles; actual cost depends heavily on destination country and duration
key_features: Overseas emergency medical and hospitalization cover
Study interruption / loss of tuition fee cover in some plans
Sponsor protection cover if the paying sponsor becomes unable to pay
Baggage delay/loss and passport loss cover
Often meets visa-mandated minimum insurance requirements for study-abroad destinations
typical_exclusions: Pre-existing conditions unless specifically declared and accepted
Treatment in a country other than the one declared on the policy
Elective or cosmetic treatment
Claims after the policy/visa period has lapsed
Mental health treatment beyond a capped limit in many plans
waiting_period_note: Many study-abroad policies have minimal or no waiting period for acute illness/accidents given the short, fixed term, but pre-existing conditions are generally excluded unless separately declared and underwritten

name: Maternity Cover Add-on
description: An add-on or rider to a base health/family-floater policy that covers delivery and related maternity expenses, relevant to married students or young married couples rather than to typical single student cover.
price_basis: approx market range for a maternity rider add-on premium on a base policy, from general comparison articles
key_features: Covers normal and C-section delivery expenses up to a sub-limit
Pre- and post-natal consultation cover in some plans
Newborn baby cover for a limited period after birth in some plans
typical_exclusions: Only available after a long waiting period (commonly 2-4 years) from the policy/rider start
Complications beyond the maternity sub-limit
Fertility treatment and related procedures (usually excluded entirely)
waiting_period_note: Maternity cover typically requires a waiting period of 2-4 years of continuous policy renewal before becoming claimable

name: Dental & Vision Add-on Cover
description: A narrow add-on covering routine dental and vision expenses (check-ups, cleaning, spectacles/lenses) that standard hospitalization policies generally exclude.
price_basis: approx market range for a dental/vision rider, from general comparison articles; sold bundled with OPD riders in many plans
key_features: Routine dental check-up and minor procedure cover
Spectacles/contact lens reimbursement up to a sub-limit
Often bundled into a broader OPD add-on rather than sold alone
typical_exclusions: Cosmetic dental procedures (e.g. whitening, veneers)
Orthodontic treatment (braces) usually excluded or heavily capped
Expenses beyond the annual sub-limit
waiting_period_note: Commonly has its own waiting period (often 30-90 days), separate from the base policy's waiting periods
